weather_report:
In Boston, the afternoon has settled into a somber embrace, a thick veil of fog rolling over the skyline, obscuring all but the most persistent outlines of familiar landmarks. Rain, persistent and heavy, taps against windows in a soothing rhythm, while the air hangs damp with anticipation—echoing the slight chance of thunder that adds a faint crackling energy to the otherwise tranquil scene. The temperature, remarkably cool, hovers in the upper sixties, inviting a snug wrap of fabric against the chill that accompanies the moisture-laden breeze. 

As twilight approaches, the fog thickens, shrouding the city in a cloak of mystery, and the forecast insists on more rain tonight—promising an inch of lively drizzle that might awaken the senses. It is not an evening for grand outings or high spirits but rather for a reflective sojourn indoors, perhaps curled up with a favorite book or engaged in the delicate artistry that awaits at the easel. Layering in soft, water-resistant garments will serve well against the elements, while a reliable umbrella could be your steadfast companion. So, as the day drifts toward nightfall, take solace in the rich sounds of rain—a gentle music that intertwines with the muted glow of city lights, inviting quiet contemplation while the world outside finds beauty in the obscured skyline.
